rated_messages.input_message: Step back from what is stressful by taking 10 slow breaths. Count them as you go and notice your breath. If you get distracted, keep starting over until you get to 10.

The best way to deal with any urges from being around smokers is to get out of the situation briefly until it goes. Make an excuse, go to the toilet, go get some water, pretend you need to get some phone reception!
Take a minute to notice what the urge feels like in your body without smoking a cigarette. Notice what is going on. See what happens. Does the urge pass?
You spent a long time training your brain to want a cig. Now you're retraining your brain, and it's natural that this might take time.
Each time you choose to not smoke after seeing someone else light up, you lessen the habit a little more.
Try to stop smoking by setting yourself a rule. For example, "IF I am tempted, THEN I will chew on some mints" - make your own rule that will work for you.
What can you do right now to break the automatic habit of smoking to help you feel better? Pause. Close your eyes. And take 10 slow breaths.
Picture the people or things you care deeply about. On a scale of 0-10, how willing are you to let this urge pass for those reasons?
Instead of lighting up a cigarette, light a scented candle or burn some incense.

Imagine walking into a social situation in three months' time as a non-smoker. Now hold that picture and imagine you're that person now. Seeing yourself as a non-smoker now can make it much easier to resist!
